Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed, homogeneous mass in the right upper lung field with smooth margins and no obvious signs of adjacent vessel invasion or pleural effusion. These radiographic features are characteristic of Pleuropulmonary Synovial Sarcoma (PPSS), which typically presents as a solitary, well-defined mass that can grow quite large before causing symptoms or showing invasive signs on plain film.
